Hi Stacy — great talking earlier. Short answers up front, then an ops handoff and next steps below.

1) Hosted numbers (typical production-ish profile, 32 prompt + 128 resp, steady-state but with short bursts):
   - p50: ~45-55ms
   - p95: ~95-110ms
   - p99: ~260-320ms
   Notes: those are measured end-to-end through our hosted API with streaming enabled (chunked transfer); numbers assume region-aware routing to us-west and that model variants are quantized equivalents to what we demoed.

2) Concurrency/streaming model:
   - We recommend a connection pool per client instance with 150-200 concurrent streaming sessions per worker; flows are multiplexed at the runtime level to avoid head-of-line blocking.
   - For your 200 concurrent client connections, map them to ~3-4 workers depending on token throughput. Streaming chunk size defaults to 64 tokens but can be tuned down to 32 to reduce tail.

3) Cold-cache behavior and KV warmup:
   - Cold-cache bursts will add an extra 40-120ms tail depending on prefix length. We support warmup probes (synthetic requests) and a sticky routing option that routes traffic to warmed replicas during ramp.

Attachments: I attached a first-pass latency_matrix_v1.csv that shows p50/p95/p99 across three traffic shapes (baseline, 1k burst, 5k short bursts) for the quantized model we discussed. Also attaching a draft POC schedule (veridian_poc_schedule.pdf).

Operational next steps (what I propose):
- Ben and I will run two short microbench runs against a synthetic traffic generator tomorrow morning (10/02) using your baseline token profile; we'll post the raw traces to the Drive link below.
- You confirm which data regions you want the POC in (us-west, us-east), and whether routing should prefer single-region for determinism.
- Procurement: once POC schedule looks OK, Marissa will send a simple SOW and we can start the onboarding checklist.

I'll keep this thread as the canonical ops handoff.

Thanks,

Hi team — adding a few technical clarifications so the POC is targeted: 

- The p95/p99 numbers Vivek listed assume request batching up to 8 requests per GPU in the steady state. If you run entirely single-request workloads the p99 can move +60-120ms depending on token distribution.
- For streaming, please confirm expected client-side chunk-ack behavior. If your client waits to ACK each chunk before requesting the next, that will amplify client-side perceived latency. Our recommendation: client should stream-append and render progressively without per-chunk ACKs.
- For the 1k -> 5k ramp, we can support the controlled increase but we need a 48-hour heads-up window so we can reserve burst capacity on Dedicated pools if needed.

Ben
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
